Producer disclosed bug in result.json:validity_notes V1, provenance.json:execution_notes, report.md Brotli Streaming API section, and corrected by removing flush() call. validity_findings.description: streaming_brotli_decompress loops process(chunk) and joins non-empty returns, but never drains internal buffer via process(b'') empty-input calls nor checks is_finished(). brotli docs note input may be buffered until enough data accumulated and output_buffer_limit draining may require empty-input calls. For tested payloads (high-entropy, GZIP-THEN-BROTLI outer brotli quality 4, BROTLI-THEN-GZIP inner brotli quality 4) no drain needed (audit independent recomputation 480/480 still matches with and without drain). Risk is bounded to untested encodings/levels where final block remains buffered and would truncate output. Ceiling bounded to tested qualities/levels.

validity_findings.description: Spec defines full-body baseline as brotli.decompress / gzip.decompress on complete compressed bytes (single-layer or sequential outer-then-inner). Implementation uses iterative fullbody_decompress(max_depth=5) trying brotli then gzip each depth. For depth-2 stacked encodings this is functionally equivalent (verified: outer brotli decompress then inner gzip decompress). For single-layer regression uses same iterative decompress which still resolves correctly (240/240). No masking of silent fallback observed (silent_fallback_count 0). Acceptable but note representation loss: iterative could theoretically decompress deeper than spec intends (depth up to 5).

Only equal chunk_size alignment tested (outer and inner both 8192 or both 32). Spec measurement_validity[7] lists chunk sizes 8192 and 32 but does not require mixed-size matrix. Parent unresolved noted mixed proxy/client chunk sizes untested. Claim ceiling correctly excludes mixed-size generalization.

claim_ceiling: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST narrowly and only at the in-process decompressor API layer: brotli.Decompressor().process(chunk) fed CHUNK_SIZE chunks (8192 and 32) and gzip.GzipFile(io.BytesIO(compressed)).read(CHUNK_SIZE) loops produce byte-identical SHA256 to full-body iterative decompression (brotli.decompress/gzip.decompress max_depth=5) for high-entropy (5.49/4.66/7.69 bits/byte) multi-layer payloads at 10KB and 100KB nominal (compressed 2.6-98.7KB) under GZIP-THEN-BROTLI (gzip level 1 -> brotli quality 4) and BROTLI-THEN-GZIP (brotli quality 4 -> gzip level 1) across 4 auth states, 3 content types, 5 reps per state (480 streaming multi-layer observations). Single-layer gzip (default level) and brotli (quality 6) validated at 10KB. Validated environment: Python 3.12.14, brotli 1.2.0, stdlib gzip, Ubuntu 24.04, single process, equal chunk sizes for outer/inner layers, sequential unwrapping. NOT validated: real CDN infrastructure (Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai) with Accept-Encoding negotiation, Vary/cache, geographic latency, TCP segmentation, concurrency; payloads >100KB (500KB/1MB); depths 3-5 stacked encodings; other gzip levels 2-9 or brotli qualities 5-11; mixed chunk sizes (e.g., proxy 8192/client 32); cross-run PYTHONHASHSEED reproducibility for BINARY; other library versions; HTTP TE framing beyond in-memory (already validated orthogonally in parent). Identity wire-preservation claim is tautological (bypassed API).
